sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining, so it throws when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, undefined, or empty. WHY: Users who select Google Meet without a connected Google Calendar now hit a TypeError instead of the previous fallback to Cal Video. HOW: Change the condition to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

WHAT: When `externalCalendarId` is omitted, the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar` for an entry whose `externalId` equals the missing value, which never matches. WHY: `updateEvent` sends `calendarId: undefined` to Google and fails; `deleteEvent` falls back to `"primary"` and can delete the wrong event. HOW: Replace the tautological find with `externalCalendarId || event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. WHY: For collective events whose organizer/eventType has no destinationCalendar, all co-host destination calendars are dropped and no calendar events are created for the team. HOW: Initialize `destinationCalendar` to `[]` instead of `null` and call `evt.destinationCalendar.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` without optional chaining.

WHAT: The organizer email is always taken from the first destinationCalendar while the event is inserted into the calendar whose `credentialId` matches the supplied credential. WHY: For collective events, creating the Google event on a co-host's calendar still labels the main organizer's calendar email as the organizer, producing mismatched event ownership and invites. HOW: Compute `selectedDestinationCalendar` as the entry matching `credentialId` and use that for the organizer email, falling back to the first entry.

WHAT: `createAllCalendarEvents` calls `prisma.credential.findUnique` once per destinationCalendar whose credential is not already in `this.calendarCredentials`. WHY: A collective event with N hosts triggers N sequential database queries, scaling linearly with host count. HOW: Collect the missing credential IDs first and load them with a single `prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: [...] } } })` before the loop. The same pattern applies to `updateAllCalendarEvents`.

WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without optional chaining. WHY: When `evt.destinationCalendar` is undefined, null, or empty, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined and booking creation crashes with a TypeError on the Google Meet fallback path. HOW: Use optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

WHAT: The fallback calendar selection compares every destination calendar's `externalId` to `externalCalendarId`, which is `null` when the caller did not supply one. WHY: `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and `calendar.events.update` receives an undefined `calendarId`, causing the update to fail or target the wrong calendar. HOW: Fall back to the main host destination calendar: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`.

WHAT: The fallback `calendarId` is computed by searching `event.destinationCalendar` for an entry whose `externalId` equals the omitted `externalCalendarId`. WHY: The comparison is always false when `externalCalendarId` is missing, so the delete falls back to `primary` instead of the destination calendar that actually owns the event. HOW: Use `const calendarId = externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`.

WHAT: The event organizer email is always taken from the first `destinationCalendar` entry, while the calendar used for insertion is selected by `credentialId`. WHY: For a team member's credential, the event is inserted into that member's calendar but the organizer email still points to the main host, misattributing ownership in invitations and calendar UI. HOW: Compute the destination matched by `credentialId` and use its `externalId` for the organizer email, falling back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar` only when no match exists.

WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. WHY: The subsequent `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a no-op in that case, so collective team members' destination calendars are silently dropped and those hosts are not invited correctly. HOW: Reassign to a new array instead of mutating: `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars];`.

WHAT: The organization create payload now sets `slug` only when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is true. WHY: This inverts the previous behavior and leaves the organization slug unset when team billing is disabled, breaking organization lookup/URL generation for self-hosted/non-billing deployments. HOW: Restore the original condition: set `slug` directly when billing is disabled and keep `requestedSlug` in metadata when billing is enabled.

WHAT: `createAllCalendarEvents` and `updateAllCalendarEvents` call `prisma.credential.findUnique` inside loops over destination calendars/references. WHY: For collective bookings each missing credential triggers a separate database round-trip, producing N+1 queries that grow linearly with the number of hosts. HOW: Collect the missing credential IDs first and load them with a single `prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: missingIds } } })` before iterating.

WHAT: When `externalCalendarId` is omitted, the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar` for an entry whose `externalId` equals the missing value, which never matches. WHY: `updateEvent` sends `calendarId: undefined` to Google and fails; `deleteEvent` falls back to `"primary"` and can delete the wrong event. HOW: Replace the tautological find with `externalCalendarId || event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

WHAT: The organizer email is always taken from the first destinationCalendar while the event is inserted into the calendar whose `credentialId` matches the supplied credential. WHY: For collective events, creating the Google event on a co-host's calendar still labels the main organizer's calendar email as the organizer, producing mismatched event ownership and invites. HOW: Compute `selectedDestinationCalendar` as the entry matching `credentialId` and use that for the organizer email, falling back to the first entry.

WHAT: The event organizer email is always taken from the first `destinationCalendar` entry, while the calendar used for insertion is selected by `credentialId`. WHY: For a team member's credential, the event is inserted into that member's calendar but the organizer email still points to the main host, misattributing ownership in invitations and calendar UI. HOW: Compute the destination matched by `credentialId` and use its `externalId` for the organizer email, falling back to `mainHostDestinationCalendar` only when no match exists.
Add optional chaining so the condition reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

Because the fallback searches `event.destinationCalendar` for an `externalId` matching the omitted `externalCalendarId`, it never matches, so `updateEvent` passes `undefined` to Google and `deleteEvent` falls back to `primary` and risks deleting the wrong event. Replace the tautological `find` with `externalCalendarId || event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.
Change the check to `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

Comparing each destination calendar's `externalId` against a missing `externalCalendarId` yields no match, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and `calendar.events.update` receives an undefined `calendarId`. Fall back to the main host destination calendar with `externalCalendarId || mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`.

issues.descricao: Claims the optional chaining in mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant because a ternary already checks it.
issues.textoGolden: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

issues.descricao: When externalCalendarId is absent, updateEvent/deleteEvent look for a destination calendar whose externalId equals that absent value, so the lookup never matches and the configured destination calendar is no longer used.
issues.textoGolden: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId` against `null`/`undefined` and matches nothing (the same wrong pattern is duplicated in deleteEvent at lines 315-317).
WHY: When `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` are called without an externalCalendarId, `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` now resolves to `undefined` instead of the host's destination calendar externalId (old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), so the Google API is invoked with an undefined calendarId and the update/delete targets the wrong (or default) calendar or errors.
HOW: Find the destination calendar for the current credential (e.g. by credentialId) rather than comparing `externalId` to the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`, or restore the single fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

Dead computation in the fallback: the else branch runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it calls `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing every cal.externalId to undefined. Nothing can match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the fallback that previously returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is lost. Match the intended criterion (destination calendar's own externalId/credentialId), not the already-falsy externalCalendarId.

Same dead-computation defect in deleteEvent: the else branch executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet the predicate `(cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against undefined and can never match, so calendarId falls through to "primary" and the event is deleted from the wrong calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar. Fix the predicate to use the destination calendar's externalId (or credentialId) rather than the falsy externalCalendarId.

issues.descricao: The organization slug is now set only when team billing is enabled (inverted condition), so with billing both slug and requestedSlug are set and without billing neither is.
issues.textoGolden: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

comentarios.texto: Organization creation no longer assigns a slug when team billing is disabled, while requestedSlug is also omitted in that mode. New self-hosted organizations therefore have neither publication field, and publish.handler rejects them because requestedSlug is missing. Restore the non-billing slug assignment.

WHAT: slug spread condition was inverted from ...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && {slug}) to ...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? {slug} : {}). WHY: organizations get slug when billing enabled and lose it when disabled, opposite of prior contract and breaking slug/requestedSlug pairing. HOW: restore negation for slug branch.

issues.descricao: Office365 (and Lark) createEvent ignore the new credentialId argument and always use the first destination calendar, so in collective bookings other hosts' credentials target the organizer's calendar instead of their own.
issues.textoGolden: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

comentarios.texto: Office365 creation always selects the first host's destination despite being invoked separately with each host's credential. A collective booking with distinct Office365 calendars sends the second host's token to the first host's calendar ID, causing failed or incorrectly targeted creation. Accept the credentialId supplied by CalendarManager and select the matching destination.

Select the destination belonging to the current credential rather than always taking the first array entry. EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination with that destination's credential, while passing the full event array each time. In a collective booking with two Outlook hosts, the second host therefore attempts to insert into the first host's calendar using the second host's token, typically failing instead of creating the second calendar event. Accept the credentialId passed by CalendarManager and match the destination by that ID (or pass a destination-specific event).

Select the destination belonging to the credential passed by CalendarManager, rather than always selecting the first array element. EventManager now invokes creation for each collective host with the full destination array. A second Office365 host therefore attempts to write to the first host's calendar using its own token, causing creation to fail or target the wrong calendar; meanwhile the saved reference records the second host's externalId.

issues.descricao: Claims updateAllCalendarEvents passes an undefined credential to updateEvent when reference.credentialId points to a credential that cannot be found.
issues.textoGolden: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

issues.descricao: The Google Meet fallback reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining, so a Meet booking with a null or empty destinationCalendar throws instead of falling back to Cal Video.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining after destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`.
WHY: The previous code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which was null-safe; now when `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets it to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one) and `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, destructuring yields `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, crashing the booking creation flow.
HOW: Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined` because `evt.destinationCalendar` may now be null or an empty array (callers such as handleNewBooking pass `: null` / `: []`). The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, but the new line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` to preserve the null-safe fallback.

The Meet-location fallback destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which this PR now produces in many callers, e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, the payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/deleteCredential/requestReschedule handlers all set `[]` when there is no destination calendar), the destructured value is `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, aborting event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` to preserve the previous optional-chained behavior.

issues.descricao: For collective events whose organizer has no destination calendar, destinationCalendar is null and the optional push drops all other hosts' destination calendars, so those hosts never get calendar events.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`.
WHY: For a COLLECTIVE event where neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, the evt field is set to `null` (lines 1063-1067), so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` of the other hosts are dropped and those hosts are never invited — defeating the multi-host support this PR adds.
HOW: Initialize to an array (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, or default the field to `[]` instead of `null`) so team destination calendars are always appended.

The optional push discards all collected team destinations when the organizer has no destination calendar. A collective booking with configured secondary hosts therefore creates none of their calendar events even though teamDestinationCalendars contains them. Initialize the array before appending the team destinations.

Initialize destinationCalendar to an array before appending collective hosts' destinations. When neither the event type nor organizer has a destination, it is set to null above, so optional push silently discards all the computed teamDestinationCalendars. Hosts with configured destination calendars consequently receive no calendar events.

issues.descricao: Video booking references are now saved without their credentialId, so cancelling the booking can no longer find the video credential and the meeting is not deleted.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the previous non-calendar fallback `result.credentialId`.
WHY: For non-calendar results (video events) `referencesToCreate` now stores `credentialId: undefined` where it previously stored `result.credentialId`, so the persisted video reference loses its credentialId; later code that looks the reference up by credentialId (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts:491-502 deleting the video meeting, or EventManager.updateLocation) can no longer resolve the credential and the meeting is not cleaned up.
HOW: Keep the fallback for non-calendar results: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. just `result.credentialId` for both branches).

The reference mapping discards credentialId for every video result. createMeeting returns the video credential ID, and handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its reference has that ID, so newly created video meetings are left behind on cancellation. Preserve result.credentialId for video results as well.

Retain result.credentialId for non-calendar references as well. The previous mapping saved the dedicated video integration's credential ID; this change unconditionally replaces it with undefined for video results, losing the association needed to identify the account that created the meeting during subsequent lifecycle operations.

issues.descricao: createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents fetch each missing host credential with a separate findUnique inside the loop instead of one batched query.

comentarios.texto:
WHAT: The new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs a `prisma.credential.findUnique` on every destination whose credential is not found in the cached `this.calendarCredentials` (line 344); the same per-reference DB lookup was added in updateAllCalendarEvents at line 517.
WHY: For collective bookings with multiple hosts this turns one in-memory lookup into up to N sequential database round-trips added to the booking-creation hot path, scaling with host count.
HOW: Resolve all missing credential ids in a single batched query (`prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: missingIds } } })`) before the loop and build a lookup map.

issues.descricao: updateLocation stores externalCalendarId and credentialId from updateEvent's result, which never returns them, so calendar references rewritten on location edit lose their calendar and credential and later updates or cancellations misroute.

comentarios.texto: updateLocation now reads externalId and credentialId exclusively from results, but CalendarManager.updateEvent returns neither field. Calendar references produced by location editing consequently lose their calendar and credential routing information, breaking subsequent updates or cancellation, particularly for secondary collective hosts. Return those fields from updateEvent or preserve them from the corresponding booking reference.

issues.descricao: Cancelling all remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking deletes only the first calendar reference of each booking, repeated once per host, so the other hosts' events stay on their calendars.

comentarios.texto: The new per-reference loop runs the recurring-series deletion branch for every host, but that branch still iterates only bookingToDelete.user.credentials and selects the first calendar reference in each occurrence. Canceling all remaining collective occurrences repeatedly deletes the owner's events while leaving secondary hosts' events untouched. For each occurrence, delete the reference matching the current host credential using the resolved calendarCredential.

For cancel-all-remaining recurring collective bookings, delete each updated booking's reference matching the current outer reference/credential. The new outer loop iterates all calendar references, but this inner block still iterates only the organizer's credentials and takes the first calendar reference of each booking. Every outer iteration therefore repeats deletion of the first host's event, while the additional hosts' recurring events remain on their calendars after cancellation.

issues.descricao: Google createEvent picks the target calendar only by matching credentialId, so destination calendars without a credentialId are ignored and events are created on the primary calendar instead.

comentarios.texto: createEvent now picks the target calendar only by matching credentialId. Destination calendars without a credentialId (handled by EventManager's integration-based branch) never match, so events are inserted into "primary" instead of the configured destination externalId as before.

issues.descricao: For destination calendars without a credentialId, createEvent is called without the externalId, so the booking reference is stored with an undefined externalCalendarId.

comentarios.texto: In the no-credentialId branch createEvent(c, event) is called without externalId, so EventResult.externalId is undefined. The booking reference's externalCalendarId, which used to come from evt.destinationCalendar.externalId, is now not stored, which breaks later update/delete targeting. Pass destination.externalId.

In the branch for destinations without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the externalId argument. CalendarManager.createEvent only returns `externalId` when it is passed in, and EventManager now stores `result.externalId` as externalCalendarId, so these booking references are saved with an undefined externalCalendarId. Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument, so the producer returns what the consumer stores.

issues.descricao: When cancelling a recurring booking with multiple calendar references, the recurring-event deletion over all remaining bookings and credentials runs once per reference, causing duplicate delete calls and errors.
loadUsers forwards raw Prisma error messages to the client in a 400 response, exposing internal model and query details.
loadUsers throws a plain Error for an empty/invalid dynamicUserList, which the catch block converts into a generic 500 'Unable to load users', hiding a client input error behind a server error.

Collective bookings now push every team member's DestinationCalendar row (externalId, credentialId, userId) into evt.destinationCalendar, and since evt is spread into the webhook payload these other members' calendar identifiers are sent to webhook subscribers.

In Google createEvent, when no destination calendar matches the credentialId, the hangout-link events.patch is called with an undefined calendarId and fails, so the Meet link is not added to the event description.
In updateAllCalendarEvents the catch block builds an error `message` that is no longer logged or used after the PR removed console.error, leaving dead code.

When updateAllCalendarEvents fails before the calendar references are loaded, its catch now returns an empty array instead of a failed result, so a failed reschedule or location update looks successful to callers.
The hidden-notes placeholder written into calendar events is a hard-coded English string not routed through i18n.

When rescheduling merges into a new booking, only the first old `_calendar` reference is deleted via `.find()`, leaving stale events on other hosts' calendars for collective bookings; iterate all old calendar references.
handleCancelBooking queries prisma.credential.findUnique once per calendar reference inside the loop instead of batching the missing credential ids into one findMany.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The health-check kill and join-time terminate guards use isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which on Linux is the default fork context and does not match the SpawnProcess instances created by get_context('spawn'). WHY: Hung flusher processes are never killed and unterminated processes survive after shutdown, so restarted children can race against the old ones and flush the same Redis segments twice. HOW: Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or simply against not being a threading.Thread) in both _ensure_processes_alive and join.

WHAT: join() breaks out of the per-process loop as soon as the global deadline expires, so any flusher processes after the first timed-out one are neither waited for nor terminated. WHY: Those leftover daemon processes keep running after the strategy's join returns, delaying clean shutdown and potentially continuing to produce segments. HOW: Do not break on deadline; instead stop waiting but still terminate every remaining process in the loop.

WHAT: Spawned flusher processes are not recognized as multiprocessing processes because the guards check `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. WHY: On Linux `multiprocessing.Process` is the default ForkProcess class, so explicit spawn processes fail the check, leaving dead/hung processes unkilled and running processes unterminated during shutdown. HOW: Replace the `isinstance` check with `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` (or `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess)`) in both the health-check kill path and the join-time terminate path.

WHAT: `join()` breaks out of the per-process loop as soon as the global deadline expires, so flusher processes after the first one are not waited for or terminated. WHY: After a timeout-consuming `next_step.join`, the remaining time may be exhausted before any process is handled; the `break` then skips all remaining processes, leaving daemon processes running and risking data loss or resource leaks on consumer shutdown. HOW: Wait each process with its own remaining timeout and remove the outer-loop break; only stop waiting on a single process when its own timeout is exhausted.

WHAT: Memory backpressure now issues one Redis `INFO` query per flusher process because each per-shard buffer calls `get_memory_info()`. WHY: All buffers share the same Redis cluster (`get_redis_client()` returns `SENTRY_SPAN_BUFFER_CLUSTER`), and `iter_cluster_memory_usage` runs `cluster.info()` per call, so the memory check grows from one cluster query per `submit` to one query per process. HOW: Collect memory info once from a single representative buffer, or deduplicate by unique Redis client before summing.

WHAT: The health-check kill and join-time terminate guards use isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process), which on Linux is the default fork context and does not match the SpawnProcess instances created by get_context('spawn'). WHY: Hung flusher processes are never killed and unterminated processes survive after shutdown, so restarted children can race against the old ones and flush the same Redis segments twice. HOW: Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or simply against not being a threading.Thread) in both _ensure_processes_alive and join.

issues.descricao: The wait_produce timer is tagged with 'shards' while sibling flusher metrics use 'shard' for the same value, so per-shard dashboards miss it.
issues.textoGolden: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.

comentarios.texto: The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with the key `"shards"`, while the other two metrics emitted in this same loop (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce` at line 185 and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` at line 195) use the key `"shard"`. All three carry the same `shard_tag` value, so this is a pure key-name disagreement: any dashboard or alert that groups/filters by the `shard` tag will silently receive no data from `wait_produce`. Rename the tag key to `"shard"` so all flusher metrics share one tag.

The `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` timer is tagged with key `shards` while every sibling metric introduced/updated in the same method (`spans.buffer.flusher.produce`, `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`) uses the singular key `shard`. Anything consuming this metric family by the `shard` tag (dashboards, alerts, tag-based aggregation) will silently receive no data for `wait_produce`, and per-shard breakdowns of produce latency will be incomplete. Change the tag to `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` so the tag contract matches the other flusher metrics.

The wait_produce timer tags with "shards", while the sibling metrics in the same loop use "shard" for the same value (shard_tag). Use one tag key, "shard", so queries and dashboards that group by it cover all of these metrics.

issues.descricao: The time.sleep(0.1) added to test_basic to let flusher threads process is a no-op because the test monkeypatches time.sleep.
issues.textoGolden: The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The added synchronization point `time.sleep(0.1)` added after the second `step.poll()` is neutralized by the test's own `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 15 (same `time` module), so it does not actually wait. WHY: The comment says it 'Give[s] flusher threads time to process after drift change', but the call is a no-op, so the test still races the background flusher thread before `step.join()` and is liable to be flaky / to not exercise the intended post-drift flush path. HOW: Use a non-monkeypatched wait (e.g. capture the real sleep before patching, or use the flusher's thread/process join, or poll until `messages` is non-empty with a real timeout).

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does not wait: line 15 of the same test does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, which replaces `sleep` on the global `time` module, so this call (and the flusher's own `time.sleep`) is a no-op. The comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is therefore false — the call returns instantly and provides no synchronisation, so the test does not actually wait for the flusher to process after the drift change. Either synchronise on a real condition (e.g. wait until the expected message is produced) or, if the original `time.sleep` is needed here, patch a module-scoped reference instead of the global `time.sleep`.

The added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the test patches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so nothing waits for the flusher threads before `step.join()` and the `messages` assertion. Replace it with a condition-based wait, such as polling until `messages` is non-empty with a deadline. Use the real sleep saved before patching if a delay is needed.

issues.descricao: The restart path only kills a hung flusher if it is a multiprocessing.Process, but spawn-context workers are SpawnProcess, so hung processes are never killed and a duplicate flusher is started for the same shards.
issues.textoGolden: Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.

comentarios.texto: The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard does not match the SpawnProcess instances created by self.mp_context.Process. When a worker hangs, the guard skips kill() and the replacement starts while the original worker remains alive, allowing overlapping flushing of the same shards if the original resumes and leaking hung workers. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or self.mp_context.Process, and kill and join the old worker before replacing it.

The workers are created with get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances; these are not instances of multiprocessing.Process (the default-context Process class). Consequently this guard skips kill() for actual production workers. When a worker hangs, the replacement starts while the original remains alive and can resume flushing the same shards. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or the spawn-context Process class for the check, and fix the identical check in join() so shutdown also terminates surviving workers.

Workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process are SpawnProcess instances, not instances of the separate multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this guard skips kill() for production workers. When a live worker exceeds max-unhealthy-seconds, the code starts a replacement and overwrites its handle while the original is still running. If the original resumes, both workers flush the same shards, and repeated hangs can exceed the configured process limit. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or explicitly distinguish threads) and stop the old worker before replacing it.

issues.descricao: join() breaks out of the per-process loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping termination of the remaining flusher processes and leaving them running after shutdown.
issues.textoGolden: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

comentarios.texto: join() breaks out of the worker loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping cleanup for every remaining worker. If next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier worker exhausts it, remaining flushers can continue running after shutdown or partition reassignment. Use the deadline only to limit waiting and still terminate and reap every remaining process.

Do not break out of worker cleanup when the join deadline expires. If the first worker consumes the timeout, the next iteration breaks before terminating that worker or any subsequent workers. They may still be blocked in Redis or producer calls despite the shared stopped flag, leaving old workers running after strategy shutdown/reassignment. Apply the deadline only to waiting, and perform termination cleanup for every worker regardless of remaining time (using a type check that recognizes spawn-context workers).
join() waits for processes sequentially against a single shared deadline and breaks without terminating remaining processes once it expires, leaking them.

issues.descricao: The SpanFlusher docstring says it creates one process per shard, but shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

comentarios.texto: The docstring says the flusher "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing," but the code at lines 60-66 shares shards across a capped number of processes (num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards)); each shard assigned via i % self.num_processes). With the new --flusher-processes default of 1, a single process handles every shard, so the documented contract is the opposite of the behaviour this PR introduces (confirmed by test_flusher_processes_limit, which asserts 4 shards served by 2 processes). Update the docstring to say shards are distributed across up to max_processes flusher processes.

The new docstring says this creates one process per shard, but workers are capped by max_processes and shards are distributed among them. In particular, the CLI default of 1 means all assigned shards share one process. Describe capped workers with potentially multiple shards per worker so callers do not rely on per-shard process isolation.

The docstring says the flusher 'Creates one process per shard', but the number of processes is capped by max_processes (--flusher-processes), and shards are shared across processes via i % num_processes. Reword it to say that shards are distributed across at most max_processes processes.

issues.descricao: max_processes uses a truthiness fallback, so --flusher-processes 0 silently becomes one process per shard instead of being rejected.

comentarios.texto: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` treats a falsy value as 'not provided'. The new `--flusher-processes` click option is `type=int`, so a user can pass `0`; that legitimate-but-falsy value is discarded and the flusher silently spawns one process per shard instead of honoring the requested limit. Use an explicit None check, e.g. `self.max_processes = max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (and validate/reject 0 upstream).

An explicit max_processes=0 is treated as an omitted limit by `or`, so passing `--flusher-processes 0` starts one process per assigned shard instead of respecting or rejecting the supplied zero limit. The CLI accepts zero as an integer and the factory forwards it unchanged. Default only when max_processes is None, and explicitly validate that supplied process limits are positive so zero cannot silently enable potentially many workers.

`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses a truthiness test, so an explicit 0 is treated as 'unset' and silently expands to one process per shard. Use `max_processes if max_processes is not None else len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and reject values below 1.

issues.descricao: A negative --flusher-processes value is not validated and makes SpanFlusher construction fail with KeyError.

comentarios.texto: `flusher_processes` is not validated to be >= 1. `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` lets a negative value through (it is truthy), so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` becomes negative and `range(self.num_processes)` is empty, leaving `process_to_shards_map` as `{}`. The following loop computes `process_index = i % self.num_processes`, which for any negative divisor is 0, so `self.process_to_shards_map[0].append(shard)` raises KeyError and the consumer fails to construct. Since `flusher_processes` is exposed as an int CLI option (`--flusher-processes`), a negative value is reachable from configuration. Guard with `max(1, self.num_processes)` / validate the input.
negative max_processes flows through `or` guard into min() -> empty map -> KeyError on i % num_processes; empty assigned_shards yields zero processes.

issues.descricao: submit() queries cluster-wide Redis memory once per flusher buffer, repeating identical INFO calls per process on every submit.

comentarios.texto: The new loop calls get_memory_info() once per flusher buffer even though SpansBuffer.get_memory_info delegates to iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client), which fetches INFO for the entire Redis cluster regardless of assigned_shards. With P flusher processes and memory backpressure enabled, each submitted batch now performs P identical cluster-wide memory queries on the consumer thread instead of one, increasing Redis traffic and blocking ingestion. Fetch cluster memory information once from a single buffer.
submit() loop calls buffer.get_memory_info() per flusher but each call is cluster-wide from same client, repeating identical INFO N× per submit.

issues.descricao: _create_process_for_shard is added but never called.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is newly added but has no caller anywhere (grep for `_create_process_for_shard(` finds only its definition); the restart path actually used is `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. WHY: This is dead code that indicates the intended per-shard restart wiring was left incomplete — any future caller relying on restarting only the process owning a given shard will silently do nothing, and it is confusing which restart path is authoritative. HOW: Remove `_create_process_for_shard`, or wire it into `_ensure_processes_alive` if per-shard restart was intended.

issues.descricao: test_flusher_processes_limit counts assigned shards instead of checking that each shard is assigned exactly once.

comentarios.texto: The assertion counts shard entries rather than verifying shard assignment. A broken distribution such as {0: [0, 1], 1: [0, 1]} still passes all assertions in this test while shards 2 and 3 are never flushed. Assert that the flattened mapping contains exactly the expected assigned shards, with no duplicates (and verify each worker's shard buffer uses that mapping), rather than only asserting a total of four.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new backup-code branch can authenticate a user without verifying the password because verifyPassword is only run when credentials.totpCode is falsy. WHY: An attacker who knows a valid static backup code can log in by also sending any non-empty totpCode, bypassing the password check entirely. HOW: Verify the password unconditionally (when the user has a CAL password) before the backup-code/TOTP branches, or require a successful password check before entering the backup-code branch.

WHAT: Backup codes are generated with crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex") (lowercase), but the server compares them with indexOf after only stripping dashes, so uppercase input never matches. WHY: A user who types or pastes a backup code in uppercase receives IncorrectBackupCode even though the code is valid. HOW: Normalize the input with .toLowerCase().trim() before the indexOf check in both next-auth-options.ts and apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts.

WHAT: After a backup code is used, the code sets backupCodes[index] = null and re-encrypts the array instead of removing the element. WHY: Once all codes are consumed the stored value is still non-empty JSON ([null,...]), so the MissingBackupCodes check never fires and the user gets IncorrectBackupCode; it also leaves stale used codes in the encrypted blob. HOW: Remove the used code with backupCodes.splice(index, 1) and throw MissingBackupCodes when the array becomes empty.

The backup-code consumption path decrypts the stored backupCodes array, validates the supplied code, mutates the matching slot to null, re-encrypts, and writes the blob back to the user row. Because this is a read-modify-write sequence with no row lock, SELECT FOR UPDATE, or atomic compare-and-swap, two concurrent login requests can read the same plaintext array, both accept the same valid code, and both issue an UPDATE that succeeds. The database serializes the writes, but each write is based on a stale pre-lock read, so one backup code can authenticate more than once, violating single-use semantics. Fix this by performing the consumption inside a transaction with a row lock (e.g., SELECT FOR UPDATE on the user row) or, preferably, by using an atomic compare-and-swap UPDATE that only succeeds if the stored encrypted blob (or a version/token) matches the value read, and verifying that exactly one row was updated. If the affected-row count is zero, the code was already consumed by another request and the current request must fail authentication.

issues.descricao: The credentials authorize() skips the password check when any totpCode is present, and the new backup-code branch never validates that totpCode, so a backup code plus a dummy totpCode logs in without the account password.

comentarios.texto: The new backup-code branch authenticates without guaranteeing the password check ran: password verification at line 121 is gated on `!credentials.totpCode`, and the branch at line 131 triggers on any truthy `credentials.backupCode` regardless of that gate. A POST to the credentials callback supplying a valid backup code together with any non-empty totpCode therefore takes the backup branch (skipping TOTP validation) while line 121 skips password verification — granting a session using only a second-factor backup code, with no account password. Require the password check before the backup branch, or include backupCode in the guard at line 121 (e.g. `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode && !credentials.backupCode)`).

The backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code even when an arbitrary nonempty totpCode has skipped password verification. The preceding guards at lines 113–125 trust the presence of totpCode, but this new branch does not validate it, allowing a holder of a backup code to log in to a password account without knowing its password by submitting both fields. Require password verification for backup-code authentication rather than allowing an unverified totpCode to bypass it.

WHAT: The new backup-code login branch authenticates without verifying the password when credentials also contain any totpCode value (password check at line 121 is skipped when totpCode is truthy, and the backup branch never checks it). WHY: An attacker holding only a backup code can add a dummy totpCode to the credentials callback and log in without the password, reducing two factors to one. HOW: Verify the password whenever backupCode is used (or decouple the password check from totpCode presence).

issues.descricao: After enabling 2FA, onEnable is only called from the backup-codes Close button; dismissing the dialog by Escape/overlay never notifies the parent, so the settings page keeps showing 2FA disabled.

comentarios.texto: On a successful enable (response.status === 200) the modal no longer calls onEnable(); it only advances to SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes, and onEnable() is now invoked solely from the 'close' button (line 269). If the user dismisses the Dialog via ESC or an overlay click, DialogContent's onOpenChange fires (wired to a plain setEnableModalOpen toggle at apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64 and the conditional render at apps/web/components/security/TwoFactorAuthSection.tsx:36), so onEnable never runs. The parent callbacks (setEnableModalOpen(false) + utils.viewer.me.invalidate() / setEnabled(true)) are skipped, leaving the 2FA Switch unchecked and the UI showing 2FA as disabled even though the server has enabled it. Call onEnable() from the dismiss path (onOpenChange) or when transitioning into DisplayBackupCodes, not only from the Close button.

Successful enablement no longer invokes onEnable until the backup-code screen's explicit Close button is clicked. Dismissing that screen through the dialog's onOpenChange instead only closes it in the parent and does not invalidate viewer.me, leaving the settings switch showing disabled even though the server has enabled 2FA. Ensure dismissal after successful enablement also invokes the completion callback and resets the setup state.

After a successful enable, `onEnable()` is no longer called and is only called from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog by Escape or overlay click (`onOpenChange`) while the codes are displayed, the parent is never notified that 2FA is enabled. The modal also keeps its step state and the plaintext backup codes. Call `onEnable` when 2FA is enabled, or make the dialog's `onOpenChange(false)` on the DisplayBackupCodes step run the same handler as Close, which resets state and clears `backupCodes`.

issues.descricao: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named TwoFactor, a copy-paste leftover from the TOTP component.
issues.textoGolden: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.

comentarios.texto: The default export is named `TwoFactor` but this file (BackupCode.tsx) renders the backup-code field and is imported as `BackupCode` by callers. The copied identifier misstates what the component is; rename the function to `BackupCode` so the name matches the file, the imports and the rendered content.

The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`, which is the name of the separate TOTP component. It is a copy-paste leftover and misleads readers and stack traces. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

Component in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor` (`export default function TwoFactor`) while the file is BackupCode.tsx and it is imported as `BackupCode`. The name disagrees with the code's contract and duplicates the real TwoFactor component, misleading callers/readers. Rename to `BackupCode`.

issues.descricao: The backup-code copy e2e test only waits for the success toast, which is shown unconditionally, so it never verifies the clipboard content.

comentarios.texto: This 'copy' test does not verify the copy behaviour it names: it clicks backup-codes-copy and then only waits for the toast-success element. The handler (EnableTwoFactorModal) runs navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) without awaiting it and then calls showToast(...) unconditionally, so the toast appears even when the clipboard write is removed or fails. The assertion therefore passes with the backup-code copy feature broken; assert the actual effect (clipboard content, or that the formatted codes reached writeText) instead of the toast.

The copy test only waits for a success toast, but the implementation emits that toast unconditionally without awaiting navigator.clipboard.writeText. Removing the clipboard write entirely, copying an empty string, or rejecting the write would still pass this test. Read the clipboard after the click and compare its contents with the displayed backup codes so the test verifies the actual copy effect.
Copy test only waits for toast-success, explicitly TODOing clipboard check. Broken writeText (wrong format/empty) still passes; assert clipboard content equals formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so concurrent logins can accept the same backup code more than once or overwrite each other's removal.
issues.textoGolden: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

comentarios.texto: Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: the code is validated with indexOf (line 144) and only then persisted via prisma.user.update (line 149), with no unique constraint or lock. Two concurrent login requests sending the same valid backup code both read the unchanged row, both pass the indexOf check, and both obtain a session, violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' invariant. Consume the code atomically (e.g. a conditional update on the raw encrypted value / a dedicated used-backup-codes table with a unique index) so only one request can succeed.

Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, breaking the stated invariant that each backup code is single-use. Two concurrent login requests with the same backup code both read the same user.backupCodes array and both pass `index !== -1` before either `prisma.user.update` commits; both then persist a stale array (each nulling only its own index), so the code authenticates twice. Make consumption atomic (e.g. compare-and-swap on the encrypted value/updatedAt, a transaction with a conditional update, or an optimistic-locking retry) so exactly one request can claim a given code.

Backup-code consumption overwrites the encrypted list by user ID without checking that the stored list still matches the value read before verification. Concurrent requests can both authenticate with the same single-use code, and requests using different codes can overwrite each other's removals and restore a consumed code. Use a conditional atomic update matching the original backupCodes ciphertext and reject or retry authentication if no row was updated.

issues.descricao: The copy button shows a success toast without awaiting clipboard.writeText, so a failed copy still tells the user their backup codes were saved.

comentarios.texto: The handler shows “Backup codes copied!” immediately after calling `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, without awaiting its promise. If clipboard access is denied or the write otherwise rejects, the user still receives a success message and may close the dialog believing their recovery codes were saved. Await the clipboard write and show the success toast only after it resolves; handle rejection with an appropriate translated failure message.

issues.descricao: The download e2e test checks only the filename, not that the file contains the displayed backup codes.

comentarios.texto: The download assertion checks only the static filename from the anchor's download attribute. It still passes if the blob contains empty or incorrect backup codes, leaving the essential recovery-code export behavior unverified. Read the downloaded file and compare its contents to the displayed codes, including their formatting.

Download test only asserts suggestedFilename, explicitly TODOing file-content check. Empty/wrong backupCodes blob with correct filename still passes; assert downloaded file lines equal displayed/formatted backup codes.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint's error log says 'backup code login' although it is disabling 2FA.
issues.textoGolden: Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

comentarios.texto: The error log says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this endpoint disables two-factor authentication and does not log in. Change the message to describe disabling 2FA with a backup code.

issues.descricao: resetState does not clear backup codes/secret or revoke the backup-codes object URL, leaving a small blob URL leaked per setup cycle.
issues.textoGolden: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: resetState() clears only password/error/step and never clears backupCodes, secret, dataUri, nor revokes backupCodesUrl. WHY: Closing the modal after setup leaves TOTP secret and backup codes in memory and leaks the Blob object URL on every setup/close cycle. HOW: Clear those states and call URL.revokeObjectURL in resetState and on unmount.

issues.descricao: The disable endpoint calls replaceAll on req.body.backupCode without checking it is a string, so non-string input throws a 500.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: req.body.backupCode.replaceAll assumes a string with no type guard. WHY: A non-string JSON value (number/array) throws TypeError and returns 500 instead of the 400 IncorrectBackupCode contract, breaking error handling and enabling error-probing. HOW: Validate typeof backupCode === 'string' (or String(...)) before replaceAll.

issues.descricao: Backup codes are matched case-sensitively against lowercase hex, so a user typing the code in uppercase is rejected.
issues.textoGolden: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

issues.descricao: The backup code is compared with the stored codes through Array.indexOf, which is not constant-time and leaks timing information about the secret backup codes.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The cleanup listener is guarded by `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) but the `management()` dispatcher returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. WHY: If both features are enabled, the listener fires and calls `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, crashing role/client/group removal. HOW: Guard the listener with the same V2-aware dispatch used by `management()`—either check V2 and route to a V2-compatible cleanup, or skip V1-style cleanup when V2 is active.

WHAT: The cleanup listener is guarded only by ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1), but management() returns the V2 implementation when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. WHY: When both features are enabled, removing a client/role/group enters the listener, calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...), and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, aborting the deletion. HOW: Guard the listener so it runs only when V1 is enabled and V2 is not, or route to a V1-only management instance inside the listener.

WHAT: The client management-permission endpoints require ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) but obtain the permission management instance through AdminPermissions.management(), which returns the V2 implementation when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. WHY: With both features enabled, calls to permissions.clients().isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled/resource/getPermissions reach ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException, returning a 500 error instead of the management reference. HOW: Use a V1-only management instance in these endpoints, or change the feature requirement to exclude the V2-enabled case.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, but AbstractTokenExchangeProvider still calls clients().canExchangeTo for client-to-client exchange, so with token exchange and FGAP V2 enabled the request fails with a server error instead of a permission decision.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, an admin granted a permission on all clients is denied on any client that also has its own per-client permission resource, because only the per-client resource is evaluated.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: getSubGroupsCount returns null when the cached group's delegate has been removed, violating the GroupModel contract that states it never returns null. WHY: Callers such as GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount propagate the null into GroupRepresentation, which can cause NPEs or incorrect serialization for consumers expecting a numeric subgroup count. HOW: Return 0L when model is null, or throw a ModelNotFoundException/IllegalStateException instead of returning null.

WHAT: The NPE fix was applied only to getSubGroupsCount; the three getSubGroupsStream overloads still dereference modelSupplier.get() without checking for null. WHY: Under the same concurrent-delete scenario the PR is fixing, these methods throw NPE when the group delegate disappears, so the fix is incomplete. HOW: Apply the same null guard (return empty stream or delegate to persistence) to getSubGroupsStream at lines 256, 262, and 268.

WHAT: The new test starts a reader thread but asserts caughtExceptions is empty without joining the thread. WHY: The reader thread may still be processing its final groups() call when the assertion runs, so exceptions thrown in that final iteration can be missed and the test can pass spuriously. HOW: Keep a reference to the Thread, call thread.join() after deletedAll.set(true), and then assert caughtExceptions is empty.

issues.descricao: The cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null when the group was deleted concurrently, violating the GroupModel contract that it never returns null and risking NPEs in callers that unbox it.
issues.textoGolden: Returning null from getSubGroupsCount() violates the GroupModel contract (Javadoc says it never returns null) and may lead to NPEs in callers that expect a non-null count.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `getSubGroupsCount()` now returns `null` when the delegate model is gone, violating the `GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount()` contract whose javadoc (GroupModel.java:296) states 'Never returns null'. WHY: In-repo callers happen to tolerate a Long null, but any caller that unboxes the result (`long c = group.getSubGroupsCount()`) or does arithmetic on it will NPE, converting the old NPE into a different one. HOW: return a non-null sentinel such as `0L` (and assert the empty/absent case explicitly), or update the interface contract to document a nullable return.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when the cached delegate is gone (modelSupplier.get() == null), whereas before this change the method delegate-called getGroupModel().getSubGroupsCount(), which could not yield null (a missing delegate surfaced as an exception instead). The declared type Long is now genuinely nullable in a path that previously always produced a value or threw, so any caller that relies on the old contract — unboxing the result (e.g. `group.getSubGroupsCount() > 0`, `long n = group.getSubGroupsCount()`, or passing it to a primitive-typed parameter) — will now throw a NullPointerException instead of getting a value or the previous exception. Since consumers were not updated for the new nullable contract, either keep the non-null behavior for callers that cannot handle null or audit/update every caller of GroupModel.getSubGroupsCount() to null-check before use.

getSubGroupsCount() now returns null when modelSupplier.get() is null, but the count is consumed as a number by brief-representation building; the sibling cache entity changed in this PR (CachedGroup) handles the same 'model unavailable' case by returning a non-null default (getRoleMappings returns Collections.emptySet(), and the subGroups/attributes loaders are built with non-null empty defaults). Returning null here breaks that convention and can surface as an unboxing/NPE on the consumer side of the read path. Return a non-null value (e.g., 0) or only null if the GroupModel contract explicitly declares it nullable.

issues.descricao: The concurrency regression test never waits for the reader thread before asserting no exceptions, so it can pass even when the concurrent-deletion NPE still occurs.
issues.textoGolden: The reader thread isn’t waited for; flipping deletedAll to true and asserting immediately can race and miss exceptions added just after the flag change, making this test flaky.

comentarios.texto: The reader thread is started but never synchronized with: the test does not wait for it to complete a read before deleting, and does not join it before asserting caughtExceptions is empty. The deletes can finish before the reader reads at all, or a failing read can land after the assertion, so the test passes even with the bug present. Use a CountDownLatch counted down after the reader's first successful read, start deleting only after it fires, and join the thread (after setting deletedAll) before asserting.

WHAT: The reader thread started at line 139-149 is never joined before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` runs. WHY: The reader can be mid-request when `deletedAll.set(true)` executes; if that request throws (e.g., reading a group deleted concurrently), the exception is appended to `caughtExceptions` AFTER the assertion has already evaluated, so the test can pass even when the NPE regression it targets is present (and is flaky). HOW: after `deletedAll.set(true)`, `thread.join(<timeout>)` (storing the Thread reference) before the assertion.

The reader Thread is started but never joined, so the assertion at line 157 can execute before the reader has completed a single groups() read (or while a read that would throw the NPE is still in flight). If the GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount null-model NullPointerException were reintroduced, this test could still pass because caughtExceptions is asserted empty before the racing reader thread has recorded anything. Capture the Thread, then join it (e.g. Thread reader = new Thread(...); reader.start(); ... deletions ...; deletedAll.set(true); reader.join();) before asserting so the test actually waits on the condition it verifies.

issues.descricao: The reader thread's stop flag is set only after all deletions succeed, so a failing delete leaves a non-daemon thread polling indefinitely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The reader loop `while (!deletedAll.get())` has no termination guarantee and `deletedAll.set(true)` at line 155 only runs after the delete loop at 152-154 completes. WHY: If any `group(groupUuid).remove()` throws, `deletedAll` is never set, so the non-daemon thread loops forever and the test JVM hangs. HOW: set the thread as daemon and/or wrap deletion in try/finally so `deletedAll.set(true)` always executes.
The test has a mid-loop abort hazard.

The reader's stop flag is set only after every deletion succeeds, with no finally block. If any remove() throws, the test exits with a live non-daemon thread that keeps issuing requests and collecting exceptions indefinitely, interfering with teardown and potentially preventing JVM termination. Put stop signaling and reader termination in a finally block around deletion.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for `scope: "team"`, allowing compile-time-valid calls that fail runtime validation and silently return `NOTHING_CONDITION`. WHY: Callers lose TypeScript protection for a required field, so a missing `teamId` is no longer caught at build time and instead yields empty results at runtime. HOW: Replace the hand-written public type with the existing discriminated union, e.g. `export type InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions = z.infer<typeof insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema>;`, so `teamId` is required exactly when `scope` is `"team"`.

WHAT: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions makes teamId optional even when scope is "team", while the runtime zod schema still requires it. WHY: A compile-time-valid call with scope "team" and no teamId fails safeParse, sets this.options to null, and silently returns NOTHING_CONDITION (1=0) instead of surfacing the error or catching it statically. HOW: Change InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions to a discriminated union matching the schema, e.g. `{ scope: "user"; userId: number; orgId: number } | { scope: "org"; userId: number; orgId: number } | { scope: "team"; userId: number; orgId: number; teamId: number }`, or keep the loose type and throw when safeParse fails.

issues.descricao: In getBaseConditions, the branches for a missing authorization condition are unreachable because getAuthorizationConditions always returns a Prisma.Sql.
issues.textoGolden: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

comentarios.texto: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches (returning NOTHING_CONDITION) in getBaseConditions can never execute. Simplify to: if filterConditions, combine it with authConditions; otherwise return authConditions.

Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions: authConditions is always a truthy Prisma.Sql object (never null, NOTHING is `1=0`), so `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else { return NOTHING }` can never execute. Simplify to if(filter) return auth AND filter else return auth, or make the nothing-case explicit.

WHAT: `getBaseConditions` returns `filterConditions` alone (no authorization predicate) when `authConditions` is falsy (`else if (filterConditions) { return filterConditions; }`). WHY: The WHERE clause returned to consumers then contains no ownership/authorization restriction, so a caller using it would return every booking matching the filters (e.g. all bookings for the given eventTypeId/memberUserId) regardless of the requesting user's org/team membership — an authorization-boundary bypass if `getAuthorizationConditions()` ever yields a falsy value. HOW: Always AND the authorization predicate with the filters and fall back to `NOTHING_CONDITION` when no auth predicate exists, e.g. `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;` (or keep the `NOTHING_CONDITION` default when auth is missing).

issues.descricao: The getBaseConditions test uses a single booking matching both auth and filter conditions, so it would pass even if the conditions were not combined.

comentarios.texto: The rewritten "should combine authorization and filter conditions" test cannot fail if the combination is broken. The fixture creates a single booking that satisfies the auth condition (userId = user.id AND teamId IS NULL) and the filter condition (eventTypeId = eventType.id) independently, so getBaseConditions returning auth-only, filter-only, or the AND combination all yield the same single-row result asserted here. Only a `1=0` result would be caught. Make the data distinguish the two: add a booking that matches the filter but not the auth (e.g. a team booking with the same eventTypeId), then assert the result excludes it, so that dropping either branch changes the returned rows.

issues.descricao: The caching tests for getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions were removed in the Prisma.sql conversion, leaving the cached-condition logic untested.
Claims getBaseConditions returns OR fragments without parentheses, so a caller appending `AND <extra>` would leak rows outside the authorization scope.
The new public options type makes teamId optional for team scope, so a missing teamId compiles and silently yields empty insights instead of a type error.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a freshly allocated TestLogger that is disconnected from the receiver's log storage. WHY: LoggerMiddleware now logs through m.logger.FromContext(ctx), so tests that inject a TestLogger into NewLoggerMiddleware cannot assert on the emitted logs because they are written to a separate instance. HOW: Return the receiver f (or a wrapper that forwards to f) so logs emitted via FromContext remain inspectable on the original TestLogger.

WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a freshly allocated TestLogger that does not share the receiver's captured log state. WHY: LoggerMiddleware now calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...), so tests injecting a *TestLogger and asserting on InfoLogs will see no captured entries because the message is written to the disconnected instance. HOW: Return the receiver (or a TestLogger that shares the same Logs fields) so log capture remains observable.

issues.descricao: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger instead of the receiver, so logs written via the contextual logger are lost to assertions on the original fake.
issues.textoGolden: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger instead of the receiver. WHY: LoggerMiddleware calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info so the write goes to a throwaway instance and assertions on the original TestLogger Calls/Message never observe it, diverging from real wrapper that preserves logger context. HOW: Return f (or a child sharing f) instead of NewTestLogger.

issues.descricao: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after the middleware was renamed to MetricsMiddleware.

comentarios.texto: TestInstrumentationMiddleware still carries the old name even though this PR renamed the middleware under test to MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware/NewMetricsMiddleware) and the file to metrics_middleware_test.go. The identifier advertises the superseded "InstrumentationMiddleware" name; rename it (e.g. TestMetricsMiddleware) so the test name matches the code it exercises.
Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware but it constructs and asserts MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware). Rename to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed middleware.

issues.descricao: The FromContext doc comment is copied from New() and misdescribes the method, which attaches attributes stored in the context.Context.
